question: The Moidams-the Mound-Burial System of the Ahom Dynasty in ______ was added to the list of UNESCO World Heritage Sites in 2024.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Moidams are also known as Maidams, which are mound-burial systems of the Ahom dynasty in Assam.
 
• These burial mounds are located in the Charaideo district of Assam.
 
• Charaideo was the original capital of the Ahom Kingdom established by Sukaphaa in 1253.
 
• In 2024, the Moidams were recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site due to their cultural and historical significance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ahom Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Ahom dynasty ruled the kingdom of Assam for nearly 600 years from 1228 to 1826.
 
• They are known for their unique burial practices and the Moidams are a testament to their rich cultural heritage.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Sites:**
 
 
• These are landmarks or areas selected by the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization for having cultural, historical, scientific, or other forms of significance.
 
• The goal is to preserve and protect these sites for future generations.
 
 
 
• **Charaideo:**
 
 
• It is known as the 'Pyramids of Assam' due to the burial mounds of the Ahom kings and queens.
 
• Charaideo was the sacred burial ground and the first capital established by the Ahom dynasty.
 
 
 
• **Burial Mounds:**
 
 
• These are raised areas of earth constructed over graves, serving as a significant cultural practice in various ancient civilizations.
 
• The Moidams of Assam are unique as they represent the mortuary practices of the Ahoms and are comparable to other global mound burial traditions.
